claim: A trusted Linux project now passes its resolved native executable PATH to Codex shell commands and its four local MCP servers. A fresh native Codex app-server loaded all five selected MCP servers, resolved all fourteen checked context-tool commands and completed five read-only MCP calls without starting a model turn.
limitations: The already-running Desktop connection was not restarted or modified through private IPC. Fresh native acceptance does not prove it reloaded; use the supported MCP Restart control or a fresh task.
The fourteen command checks establish executable discovery, not fourteen new install/use/lifecycle tests. Other functional acceptance remains dated and separately scoped.
The same-process jCodeMunch increment is a bytes/4 estimate including this validation call; it is not provider-token savings. Do not add session and retained values.
No fake global session identifier was introduced. Shared Context Mode parent-PID statistics and unscoped Desktop Prometheus series remain unattributed.
OmniRoute stays optional with compression off. Account quotas, rejected compression fidelity and unsupported encrypted restore are unaffected.
Local private account/configuration files, command search paths and raw MCP inventories are not portable artifacts. Resolve the target host's paths and use its own native sign-in.
Zero provider turns refers to this isolated configuration/MCP acceptance harness, not the surrounding authoring conversation.

execution.command_note: Recorded authoring-host invocation with the already-selected local permission policy; not a recommended permission default. PROJECT_ROOT substitutes the private resolved path.

private_evidence.publication_policy: Raw config, inventory, tool responses and native execution remain private; hashes bind retained authoring-host bytes without exposing account or path data.
